note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  New dry, red, itchy skin on hands and arms for a few days, noticed after swimming; coconut butter not helping. No fever, no sweating, no vomiting, normal appetite, normal bowels and urine. Feels tired. Work-related stress and long hours.
- Relevant family medical history:  Father: asthma. Mother: hayfever. No known family skin disease.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Coconut butter topical use — dose/route/frequency not documented. Allergies: possible lactose intolerance; no medication allergies documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Using combined oral contraceptive (Microgynon). No further sexual health history recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Appetite normal; otherwise not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Does not smoke. No alcohol. No recreational drug use.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Reports increased work-related stress; no depression or self-harm screening documented.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives alone. Primary school teacher. No caring responsibilities recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- 26-year-old woman with acute pruritic, erythematous, dry dermatitis on hands and arms beginning a few days ago, temporally associated with swimming. No systemic symptoms. No prior eczema; family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever). Work stress present; patient feels tired.
- Working diagnosis: Dermatitis, most consistent with irritant contact dermatitis from pool chemicals (chlorine) given timing and distribution.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — High likelihood: onset after swimming; hands/arms exposed; pruritic, red, dry skin; no systemic features.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood: possible sensitivity to pool disinfectants or personal care products; lacks clear new product trigger.
  - Atopic dermatitis (adult-onset/exacerbation) — Moderate likelihood: family atopy and stress; first episode and sharp temporal link to exposure make contact dermatitis more likely.
- Management priorities: Reduce inflammation and itch; restore skin barrier; monitor response; reassess if not improving or worsening.

Management Plan

- Topical therapy: Recommend emollients applied frequently through the day; topical steroid cream offered/recommended for inflamed areas (potency not documented).
- Symptom relief: OTC antihistamines suggested (e.g., Piriton/chlorphenamine or loratadine) for itch.
- Education: Provided patient information on dermatitis and skin care.
- Medications to avoid: Analgesics (e.g., paracetamol) not indicated for itch.
- Follow-up: Return next week if not improving, or sooner if worsening/spreading or systemic symptoms develop.
- Investigations/referrals: None ordered; not recorded.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Dermatitis review advised next week if not improving; other preventive follow-ups not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Irritant contact dermatitis — High: Clear temporal link to swimming; hands/arms involvement; pruritic, erythematous, dry skin; no systemic symptoms.
- Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate: Possible reaction to pool chemicals/soaps; limited to exposed areas; no definitive new product identified.
- Atopic dermatitis (adult-onset) — Moderate: Pruritus and family atopy; stress as trigger; first episode and exposure-related onset favor contact dermatitis over atopic dermatitis.

Quality checks

- Missing elements: BP, pulse; height/weight/BMI/waist; oral/ear/vision exams; urinalysis; immunization review; cervical screening status; STI risk and screening; fasting/random BGL and lipid profile; other relevant labs; detailed allergy history (drug/food); physical activity and diet assessment; depression/anxiety/self-harm screening; hearing concerns; social supports/caring responsibilities; Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status and CTG eligibility.
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Telehealth consultation with no physical exam; several brief inaudible/unfinished responses but core history captured.
